class.name: GameplayTagContainer
class.brief_description: An ordered set of gameplay tags, serialized as plain names.
class.description: Serializes as a [PackedStringArray] of tag names and resolves each name through [GameplayTagsManager] on load. That is deliberate: assets reference tags by name, so a tag can move between tables, or a table can be split, without touching anything that uses it. [method has_tag] honours the hierarchy - a container holding [code]A.B.C[/code] answers yes to [code]A.B[/code]. The exact variants do not.

method.name: add_tag
method.description: Adds [param tag]. Adding a tag already present does nothing.

method.name: add_tag_by_name
method.description: Adds the tag called [param tag_name], resolving it through [GameplayTagsManager].

method.name: get_length
method.description: How many tags the container holds.

method.name: get_tag
method.description: The tag at [param index], or null when the index is out of range.

method.name: has_all
method.description: True if this container holds every tag in [param tag_container], hierarchically.

method.name: has_all_exact
method.description: As [method has_all], but every match must be exact.

method.name: has_any
method.description: True if this container holds at least one tag from [param tag_container], hierarchically.

method.name: has_tag
method.description: Hierarchical test: a container holding [code]Status.Debuff.Burning[/code] answers true for [code]Status.Debuff[/code]. This is almost always the one you want.

method.name: has_tag_exact
method.description: As [method has_tag], but only an exact name counts.

method.name: remove_tag
method.description: Removes [param tag]. Removing one that is not present does nothing.

members.member: The container's contents as plain names. This is the serialized form: tags are stored as strings and resolved through [GameplayTagsManager] on load, so a tag can be renamed or moved between tables without touching the assets that use it. [b]Never author an inline [GameplayTag] sub-resource in a .tres[/b] - it compares equal by name but is not the canonical instance.
